intervals.label: approval of the BEPC Upgrade Project
intervals.quote: In December 2003, the National Development and Reform Commission officially approved the BEPC Upgrade Project.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: IHEP history page (timeline); end = first collisions in July 2008
intervals.note: End is the month of the first BEPCII collisions (July 2008).
intervals.quote: In January 2004, the BEPC Upgrade Project kicked off.

intervals.label: commissioning
intervals.locator: IHEP history page (timeline); end = acceptance test, July 2009
intervals.note: The National Acceptance Test was passed in July 2009.
intervals.quote: In July 2008, the first collisions took place at BEPCII, the upgraded BEPC, and were observed by the new BESIII detector.

intervals.label: e+e- collider operation
intervals.locator: IHEP history page (timeline); end from the IPAC'26 paper (shutdown of BEPCII on July 1st, 2024)
intervals.note: Design luminosity was reached in April 2016 (IHEP history page). Start = acceptance test; physics data taking with BESIII had begun with the July 2008 collisions.
intervals.quote: In July 2009, the Upgrade Project, BEPCII, successfully passed the National Acceptance Test organized by the National Development and Reform Commission

intervals.label: BEPCII upgrade: hardware replacement
intervals.locator: Geng et al., IPAC'26 WEP1606, abstract
intervals.note: Hardware replacement finished by the end of 2024; the end of this interval is the start of machine commissioning in May 2025 (same abstract).
intervals.quote: The upgrade of Beijing Electron and Positron Collider-II (BEPCII) has begun since the shutdown of BEPCII on July 1st in 2024.

intervals.label: commissioning of the BEPCII upgrade
intervals.locator: Geng et al., IPAC'26 WEP1606, abstract
intervals.note: The same paper reports that the designed luminosity of 1.1 × 10^33 cm^-2 s^-1 was achieved on 28 April 2026. Resumption of BESIII physics data taking is not stated in the sources fetched.
intervals.quote: the machine commissioning of BEPCII Upgrade project has started since May 2025 after recovery from the cryogenic system fault.

name: Beijing Electron-Positron Collider II
notes: The BEPCII-U target parameters (beam energy up to 2.8 GeV, luminosity gains) appear in the IPAC'26 paper tables; they are not recorded as specs because the paper is a preliminary proceedings file.

cms_energy.note: Centre-of-mass energy range 2.0-4.2 GeV; the maximum is recorded.
cms_energy.quote: running in the tau-charm energy region (Ecm = 2.0-4.2 GeV)

peak_luminosity.note: Design value at a beam energy of 1.89 GeV; IHEP reports the design luminosity was reached in April 2016.
peak_luminosity.quote: with a design luminosity of 1 × 1033 cm-2s-1 at a beam energy of 1.89 GeV

summary.plain: The rebuilt two-ring electron-positron collider at the Institute of High Energy Physics in Beijing, running in the tau-charm energy region from 2008. It hosts the BESIII detector. Since July 2024 it has been undergoing an upgrade to higher energy and luminosity, which was in commissioning in 2026.
summary.technical: BEPCII: two-ring e⁺e⁻ collider, Ecm 2.0-4.2 GeV, design luminosity 1×10³³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ at 1.89 GeV beam energy (reached April 2016); first collisions July 2008 observed by BESIII; shut down 1 July 2024 for an upgrade (BEPCII-U) to raise beam energy and luminosity; machine commissioning from May 2025, design luminosity of the upgraded machine reported achieved on 28 April 2026.
